title: Throughput evidence kit and tenant conformance protocol
creator: Anika Rao
description: Create a reproducible, tenant-aware evidence kit for certifying dedicated capacity throughput guarantees. This ticket covers a test runner, scenario library, measurement methodology, dashboards/queries, and a customer-facing acceptance checklist that together demonstrate SLA attainment for new Dedicated pools and model variants. The output is intended for SRE/solutions-engineering to run with customers during onboarding and for the platform team to validate releases.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable test run produces an immutable evidence bundle (logs, dashboards, artifacts) for each validated pool and model variant.
Defined pass/fail thresholds are encoded for the suite: sustained throughput within 5% of target for 30m, p95 tail within configured SLOs, and no node-level OOMs or GPU stalls during the run.
Autoscaler behavior is exercised and observed: scale-up events within <60s of sustained breach, scale-down cooldown respected, and no cascading pod restarts under burst traffic.
Tenant isolation test proves QPS isolation: synthetic noisy neighbor injects 2x background load and primary tenant sustains >=90% of baseline throughput.
Customer acceptance checklist drafted and validated with Solutions Eng for two pilot customers, with clear artifact locations and runbook steps.
End-to-end documentation and a CI job exist to run a lightweight smoke variant on every runtime release.
All metrics surfaced in the Console (per-route and per-tenant): QPS, tokens/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit-rate, batch size distribution, GPU utilization, and preemption events.
test_scenarios: Baseline sustained: ramp to target QPS over 5m, sustain for 30m to validate steady-state throughput and resource utilization.
Burst profile: 5x short bursts (60s) spread across different nodes to validate autoscaler ramp and tail latency under microbursts.
Noisy neighbor: inject background tenants at 50% and 200% of their nominal profiles while measuring primary tenant degradation.
Cold-start + KV priming: start with empty KV cache, run a warmup traffic pattern, verify performance delta and warmup curve to steady-state.
Long-tail stress: 6h mixed workload with variable seq lengths (16/64/512 tokens) to observe long-term drift, memory growth, and quantization path stability.
Autoscaler safety: deliberately trigger scale events and ensure rolling updates/canary routing honor fallback policies without request loss.
Failure injection: simulate a GPU node outage and observe routing fallback, retry behavior, and recovery timelines.
measurement_methodology: Deterministic driver: test runner replays pre-recorded request mixes (tenant-aware) with timestamped IDs to ensure reproducibility.
Metric collection: Prometheus scrape with high-fidelity histograms for latency and custom exporters for batch/kernel metrics; logs pushed to S3 as compressed artifacts.
Run tagging: every run is assigned a UUID and metadata (model, runtime, pool-size, quantization) to correlate dashboards and logs.
Analysis scripts: post-run validation computes sustained QPS, latency percentiles, batch-size heatmap, and KV cache heatmap. These generate a single HTML evidence page.
Noise floor control: calibrate driver network and client machine to ensure driver-side saturation does not limit observed throughput; include driver health checks.
Statistical confidence: runs repeated 3 times; median chosen and variance reported. Outlier runs flagged for investigation.
Artifact immutability: evidence bundles (dashboards, Prometheus snapshots, raw traces, runner logs) are archived to a timestamped S3 path for signoff.
deliverables: A git repo (internal) with: test runner, scenario definitions, k8s manifests for synthetic clients, and analysis scripts.
Console dashboards and saved queries for evidence visualization (per-route, per-tenant views).
A lightweight CI smoke job that runs a 5m sanity check on PRs to runtime/serving and fails on obvious regressions.
Customer-facing acceptance checklist and runbook that Solutions Eng can use during pilots.
Run templates for three common customer profiles: small (1-2 GPU), medium (8 GPU), large (64+ GPU).
A postmortem template for any failed certification runs with guided remediation steps.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Spike completed comparing existing load drivers (Locust, k6, custom Go runner). Selected custom Go runner for low jitter and precise token pacing. - Anika
2026-03-03: Drafted scenario library and initial pass at pass/fail thresholds with SRE. Targets: sustain 95% of requested QPS for 30m; p95 < 250ms for 128-token workloads. - Miguel
2026-03-07: Initial runner prototype can drive tenant-aware mixes and tag runs. Pushed repo skeleton and CI smoke workflow. - Miguel
2026-03-09: First pilot run against staging dedicated pool. Observed autoscale lag ~110s for large bursts; created follow-up ENG ticket to tweak controller scale window. - Anika
2026-03-10: Prepared customer acceptance checklist and uploaded dashboard template to Console. Scheduling pilot validation with Solutions Eng and Customer A for week of 2026-03-15. - Miguel
blocking_items: Autoscaler knobs for fast-path scale-up are gated behind ENG-271394 (controller tuning).
Need a test fleet with deterministic network topology for noisy-neighbor tests (infra provisioning request submitted).
Access to Customer A dedicated pool for pilot (Solutions Eng coordinating).
comments: Miguel (2026-03-04): We should include batch-size distribution as a primary KPI — it explains variance between runs and helps tune the kernel selector.
SRE-Lead (2026-03-05): For noisy-neighbor tests, ensure we test both CPU and GPU oversubscription — different failure modes emerge.
Solutions Eng (2026-03-08): Add a customer-friendly summary page that includes plain-language pass/fail and next steps. Customers don't need raw histograms by default.
Anika (2026-03-09): Flagging autoscaler lag as a risk for acceptance. If we can't meet the <60s target we'll need to document fallback policies and set customer expectations.
